note: WHAT A SCRUB COSTS (201/8-03). The step owes 'the frame cost of a scrub — a drag re-solves every entity, and it must not stall'. A desk run in Node against the real `BoardHistory`: a whole 8 h shift recorded at the app's 20 Hz with 150 units and 40 calls, then 300 resolves spread across the full span, which is the worst a drag can be (every frame lands on a different part of the history, so nothing is warm). No GPU and no device — what is measured is the resolve, not the paint.

load.note: 49 status transitions per call over 8 h is a deliberate over-estimate — a real call changes state a handful of times. The event list is the pessimistic half of this measurement.

readings.what: one `BoardHistory.at(t, live)` — every unit resolved from its track, every call from its event list

findings: **p50 0.071 ms, p95 0.193 ms, worst 0.636 ms.** Against a 16.7 ms frame that is 0.4 % typical and 3.8 % worst — a drag re-solves the whole board every frame and does not come close to stalling it.

The resolve is a binary search per unit over its ring plus a linear walk of each call's event list. The units are the cheap half; the pessimistic 49-transitions-per-call event lists are what the tail comes from.

**Nothing downstream of the resolve changed to make a scrub work.** The map loop, the symbology, the panels and the detail card take the board they always took — replay hands them a reconstructed `Operations` of the same shape. That is what 8/01 bought by keeping time OUT of `Unit` and in a store beside it.

The call event list is the one structure here that is NOT bounded: the unit rings are fixed-size, the events grow with the shift. At the absurd rate measured above they are 1 960 events = ~125 kB, so nothing needs doing — but a feed that flapped a call's status would grow it without limit, and that is the condition to watch.
openQuestions: What a drag costs on the PHONE. The arithmetic cannot differ, but a Mali-G51's single-thread speed is not this container's — 2/03's capture carries the `tracks` block, and a scrub during that run is the reading.

Whether React's re-render on each scrub frame is the real cost rather than the resolve. The panels re-render on every clock change and nothing here measures that; the loop itself is unaffected, since it reads through a getter.
